classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied right triangle to calculate the vertical rise, then recognise that the requested ground height also includes the 1.2 m hand height.

inlines.text: Oliver holds the end of the string of a kite 1.2 m above the ground.
The string is 30 m long and the horizontal distance to the kite is 18 m.
Find the height of the kite above the ground.

spec.description: Oliver at the lower left holds a string leading to a kite at the upper right. The horizontal leg begins at hand height. The dashed vertical extends from the kite to the ground, while a separate dimension h measures the full height.
spec.mathematics: The right triangle has hypotenuse 30 m and horizontal leg 18 m. Its vertical leg excludes the 1.2 m hand height. The full height h includes that additional 1.2 m. Diagram proportions follow the source schematic rather than a scale construction.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown h are visible; no calculated lengths are shown.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the vertical distance from Oliver’s hand to the kite. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}
x^2+18^2&=30^2\\
x^2+324&=900\\
x^2&=576\\
x&=\sqrt{576}\\
x&=24.
\end{align*}$$
Add the height of Oliver’s hand:
$$\begin{align*}
h&=24+1.2\\
h&=25.2\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
